title: Ops Scout: Hyperflow admin utility integration for guided runbooks-as-tasks
creator: Marina Alvarez
description:
Goal: Ship an integrated admin utility called 'Ops Scout' that converts curated runbooks into interactive, RBAC-scoped micro-tasks and surfaces contextual telemetry snapshots to support on-call and first-line responders. This ticket builds the integration with the Hyperflow orchestration layer so runbooks can be executed as idempotent tasks with dry-run validation, ephemeral credentialing, and structured outcome reporting. The integration must keep privileged operations gated behind scoped approvals and emit evented traces for Console observability.

Why: Current runbooks are text+checklist artifacts; responders need reproducible, auditable, and automatable task steps that can run safely in ephemeral sandboxes with clear failure modes and rollback suggestions. Ops Scout unifies admin utilities, runbooks-as-tasks, and support automation to reduce MTTI and human error while retaining operator control.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full UI surfaces in Console (thin UX hooks only), nor does it add new cryptographic KMS integrations (uses existing KMS paths).
acceptance_criteria: Runbook YAML -> Hyperflow task bundle translation succeeds for 95% of curated runbook patterns
Tasks execute in ephemeral sandbox with RBAC-scoped credentials and produce structured JSON outcomes
Dry-run mode validates preconditions without mutating infra and returns a deterministic validation report
Every executed task emits Console-compatible traces and a tokenized telemetry snapshot for later replay
Approval gating works end-to-end: attempt -> require approval -> execute -> audit log entry created
Automated rollback hook runs on failure and surfaces suggested remediation steps in the task outcome
tasks: Design Hyperflow task schema mapping for runbook primitives (create, patch, query, rollback)
Implement translator that converts runbook YAML/MD to Hyperflow bundles with metadata and provenance
Wire ephemeral credential flow and RBAC enforcement using existing admin-token service
Add dry-run validator that simulates steps and returns action-level validation reasons
Emit telemetry snapshot after each step: metrics, logs digest, pre/post resource diff
Integrate approval gate with approvals-service and create audit log entries
Add unit and e2e tests for common runbook templates and failure paths
Create minimal Console hook endpoints for task listing and outcome ingestion

2025-02-18 - Devon Park: Prototype translator committed on feature/translators/ops-scout. Basic YAML->bundle mapping works for create/patch steps. Filing follow-up for dry-run semantics.
2025-02-24 - SRE Review: Raised concern about telemetry snapshot size. Proposed digesting logs + sampling traces. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-03-02 - QA: Added e2e plan to validate approval gating under race conditions. Noted two failure modes for rollback hook needing clearer idempotency guarantees.
2025-03-05 - Devon Park: Integrated approvals-service; started wiring audit log entries. Opening PR for ephemeral credential flow. Next: add dry-run validation tests and telemetry digest logic.
notes: Implementation decisions: use Hyperflow's existing schedulers to respect latency SLOs; translator will emit 'optimistic' and 'safe' variants of bundles to allow canary-run policies.

Trade-offs: Ephemeral sandboxes will be lightweight containers with read-only mounts where possible to reduce blast radius; some legacy runbook steps require privileged host access and will be surfaced as 'blocked' unless explicit admin token is used.
Follow-ups: PM to collect top 10 runbooks used in last 6 months for templating; Design to prototype compact task UX in Console after backend hooks land.
